notes: §1985:XVI.3.2.3 SR2: "If the segment-number is omitted from the section header, the segment-number is assumed to be 0", a fixed permanent segment that keeps its last-used state. sectionDefinition and declarativeSection make the number optional, the 85 gates (VisitSectionDefinition, VisitDeclarativeSection) check only a written one, and an unnumbered section is resident like any fixed segment (AlterSwitchEmitter). The witness ALTERs an unnumbered section from segment 10 and re-enters it: FIRST, ALTERED. Probes: r7a (unnumbered main, sub and declarative sections, sequential file with a failed OPEN, independent segment 55 between) FIRST / IN 55 / DECL 35 / ALTERED / AFTER OPEN 35 / ALTERED; r6b unnumbered S0 PERFORMing segment 70 Y ALTERED; r5h `SECTION .` accepted as the omitted form; class c --std 2002 refuses only a written number (r2f COBOL0902 on numbered sections).

next.reason: 1985: "If the segment-number is omitted from the section header, the segment-number is assumed to be 0."; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the Segmentation feature; no candidate covers segment-numbers in section headers.". No 2023 clause holds segment-numbers. The wording candidates give other defaults (PAGE, LINE, ACCESS MODE, TEST BEFORE), so 2023 lacks the segmentation feature.
